[DIN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06978) already conditions history pooling on the candidate through a learned local activation unit. [DARE](https://ise.thss.tsinghua.edu.cn/~mlong/doc/Long-Sequence-Recommendation-ICLR25.pdf), ICLR 2025, explicitly separates attention embeddings from representation embeddings to reduce gradient interference; it also studies smaller attention dimensions. Thus, shared query/key item embeddings plus separate source-value and target tables closely resemble established candidate attention and embedding decoupling. A last-ten-interaction residual on SASRec is an architectural combination; these precedents weaken claims that either mechanism alone is novel.

[FPMC](https://archives.iw3c2.org/www2010/pub/pdfs/RendleFreudenthaler2010-FPMC.pdf) combines user–target preference with directional source–target transition factors. [FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.09152v1) combines history-based item similarity with higher-order transitions, using global and user-specific lag weights. Their pooling weights are candidate-independent, although their scores depend on the target. Separate source/target tables therefore also introduce established asymmetric transition capacity. FOSSIL ties long-term and transition factors to reduce parameters under sparsity. DIN’s mini-batch-aware regularization penalizes active rare-feature embeddings more strongly using inverse-frequency scaling; this is a relevant control alongside ordinary L2, embedding dropout, and table tying, without filtering benchmark items.

Suggested controls: retain identical source/target tables and replace candidate attention with uniform, learned lag-only, or user-conditioned weights; compare last-item, last-ten mean, and lag-weighted transition residuals. Use the same scoring head throughout. Compare tied versus decoupled tables, projection-based versus independent embeddings, and smaller attention dimensions. Match actively trained parameter budgets and tuning effort, rather than adding unused parameters; separately match compute. Evaluate residual-only and SASRec-plus-residual models, window sizes, and within-window order shuffling. Report fixed macro validation HR@10 plus diagnostic breakdowns by training item frequency and previously observed source–target pairs to distinguish candidate conditioning from capacity and transition memorization.
